LH-REG-003.question: An insurer incorporated in Ohio has received a certificate of authority from Pennsylvania and sells policies there. In Pennsylvania, it is considered:

LH-GEN-017.explanation: Estoppel prevents a party from reasserting a right after its own conduct led the other party to rely on it giving that right up. By accepting late premiums for two years, the insurer led the owner to rely on that practice, so a court bars the lapse. Indemnity is the principle of restoring an insured to the pre-loss condition and has nothing to do with this dispute.

LH-REG-005.explanation: Section 696-A of Pennsylvania's Insurance Department Act makes a producer a fiduciary for premiums, who may not mingle them with her own funds without the insurer's express consent; doing so is commingling and can lead to license discipline. No grace window makes depositing premiums in a personal account acceptable.

LH-PROV-004.explanation: Pennsylvania requires a grace period of 30 days or one month (Insurance Company Law section 410(b)), so the policy was still in force on March 20. The insurer pays the face amount minus the overdue premium: $100,000 - $1,200 = $98,800, not the full $100,000.

LH-PROV-005.explanation: Pennsylvania requires a reinstatement provision allowing application within three years of default (Insurance Company Law section 410(k)), with evidence of insurability and overdue premiums plus interest. Paying only the missed premium is not enough, and a surrendered policy cannot be reinstated.

LH-HPRV-006.question: Four years after issue, an insurer learns that an applicant made an innocent misstatement on her health application. Under the time limit on certain defenses provision, the insurer:
LH-HPRV-006.explanation: Pennsylvania's time limit on certain defenses runs three years from the date of issue (Insurance Company Law section 618(A)(2)); after that, misstatements other than fraudulent ones cannot be used to void the policy or deny a claim. Four years have passed, so the insurer can neither rescind nor reduce benefits for the innocent misstatement.
